name: Jezero Crater Delta — Entry Region
description: PLACEHOLDER — Jezero Crater was selected as the Perseverance landing site due to evidence of an ancient river delta, suggesting habitable conditions. This record represents the general landing site area; specific panoramas require NASA PDS data integration.

name: Gale Crater — Mt. Sharp Base
description: PLACEHOLDER — Gale Crater contains a 5 km central mound (Aeolis Mons / Mt. Sharp) with exposed sedimentary layers representing billions of years of Martian geological history. Curiosity has been exploring the crater since 2012.

name: Olympus Mons — Summit Caldera
description: PLACEHOLDER — Olympus Mons is the largest volcano in the solar system at approximately 21 km in height and 600 km in diameter. This record represents the summit caldera region. Surface observations require future robotic or human missions.

name: Valles Marineris — Canyon System Overview
description: PLACEHOLDER — Valles Marineris is a system of canyons spanning over 4,000 km in length and up to 7 km in depth. It dwarfs Earth's Grand Canyon in scale and is one of the most dramatic geological features in the solar system.

name: Hellas Planitia — Impact Basin
description: PLACEHOLDER — Hellas Planitia is one of the largest impact craters in the solar system at approximately 7,100 km in diameter and 7 km deep. Its atmospheric pressure at the bottom is significantly higher than average Martian surface pressure.
